status: frozen survey- and observable-level admission protocol; no new galaxy velocity target, action, or universal constant opened or selected
purpose: Require the frozen Sigma metric to transfer beyond spent SPARC and LITTLE THINGS evidence across galaxy mass, gas fraction, surface brightness, bulge geometry, environment, spatial resolution, radial and vertical dynamics.

spent_galaxy_evidence.role: development, morphology diagnosis and fixed-MOND comparator benchmarking; never a new holdout
spent external rotation-curve, velocity-field and simulator commissioning evidence; never a new holdout
spent pressure-supported giant-galaxy development evidence; never a new holdout

public_candidate_universes.strength: homogeneous H I tilted-ring models, rotation curves, H I surface-density profiles, geometry and two-component velocity uncertainties in three environments
public_candidate_universes.limitation: many galaxies are only marginally resolved; fixed 10 km/s dispersion, beam smearing, inclination and inner surface-density systematics must be propagated or re-forward-modeled

public_candidate_universes.strength: roughly 150-pc CO rotation curves and orientations for massive star-forming disks, resolving bulges, bars and inner baryonic structure
public_candidate_universes.limitation: CO generally probes inner disks and many systems may overlap earlier galaxy samples, so identity freshness and outer-radius coverage must be audited before holdout use
public_candidate_universes.role: high-resolution inner-geometry candidate or locked systematic test

public_candidate_universes.strength: nearly face-on disks with rotation curves, surface-brightness profiles and line-of-sight stellar velocity-dispersion profiles
public_candidate_universes.limitation: stellar scale height and mass-to-light ratio are important measurement nuisances and published availability must be verified per object
public_candidate_universes.role: radial-versus-vertical consistency candidate or locked systematic test

admission_sequence.name: identity_and_overlap_audit
admission_sequence.allowed: survey identifiers, aliases, coordinates, environment, imaging coverage and prior project use
admission_sequence.forbidden: rotation speeds, velocity fields, dispersions, residuals and halo-fit outcomes

admission_sequence.name: source_side_stratification
admission_sequence.allowed: distance priors, photometric morphology, stellar light, H I column density, gas fraction, surface brightness, bulge fraction, beam, PSF and masks
admission_sequence.forbidden: selecting galaxies because a gravity formula fits or fails their kinematics

admission_sequence.name: baryon_and_nuisance_readiness
admission_sequence.allowed: stellar-population priors, gas conversion, distance and inclination covariance, scale height, asymmetric-drift prescription and source-file hashes
admission_sequence.forbidden: per-galaxy gravity amplitudes, ranges, exponents or object labels

admission_sequence.name: freeze_sample_and_sealed_targets
admission_sequence.allowed: galaxy IDs, strata, source manifests, target product types and sealed target-file hashes
admission_sequence.forbidden: opening kinematic target contents before one action and universal constants are frozen

admission_sequence.name: open_once_and_score
admission_sequence.allowed: score circular speeds, raw velocity fields and vertical dispersions with frozen physics and a frozen nuisance policy
admission_sequence.forbidden: changing the action, constants, sample, strata or scoring rule after any target is opened

systematic_controls.requirement: For the raw subset, convolve the predicted velocity field and gas distribution through the released cube geometry and beam rather than comparing only deprojected catalog speeds.
systematic_controls.failure_meaning: A catalog-curve success that disappears in the observed cube may be inclination, beam-smearing or fixed-dispersion leakage rather than gravity.

systematic_controls.requirement: Report bulged, barred and unbarred inner residuals separately at the released CO resolution and never treat inner-only success as an outer flat-curve test.
systematic_controls.failure_meaning: A field insensitive to baryonic geometry will wash out the resolved inner features that motivated a source-state response.

systematic_controls.requirement: Use one metric and one stellar-population nuisance ensemble for both radial rotation and vertical dispersion; scale height may not be tuned to rescue gravity.
systematic_controls.failure_meaning: A law that increases radial attraction but overpredicts vertical restoring force has the wrong three-dimensional geometry even if its rotation curve looks good.

nuisance_boundary.rule: Measurement nuisances may vary only under the same external priors for every comparator. No nuisance may select or alter a Sigma gravity constant per galaxy.

priority.first: freeze and test broad galaxy and cluster transfer from one metric
priority.next: weak lensing and merger offsets, then satellite, stream and friction predictions
priority.later_hard_veto: Solar-System, PPN, propagation, stability and causal initial-value constraints

claim_boundary: This protocol identifies candidate surveys and mandatory diversity; it does not claim that 48 eligible fresh galaxies have already been assembled.
WALLABY catalog rotation curves are not raw truth: beam, inclination, fixed dispersion and tilted-ring assumptions must be audited with forward cube tests.
PHANGS inner curves and DiskMass vertical dispersions are complementary geometry tests, not substitutes for outer H I curves.
No new velocity, dispersion or residual target was opened and no galaxy was selected because of a Sigma outcome.
Solar tests remain mandatory but do not drive the current galaxy/cluster formula search.
